description: The Met Office Space Weather Operations Centre publishes a public space weather forecast for the United Kingdom and the world, together with current space weather notifications, aurora forecasts for the northern and southern hemispheres, and a forecast overview with a headline, an analysis of activity over the past 24 hours and the outlook for geomagnetic storms, solar radiation storms and radio blackouts. The page read on 26 September 2026 carried a forecast issued at 14:46 GMT with a chance of G1 minor storms from fast solar winds. Automated alerts and warnings are posted on social media, and users with a sector interest can request a specialist space weather account for tailored services. Licence (read on the provider page on 2026-09-28): Crown Copyright (Met Office information; reuse licensed by the Met Office under its terms). Access is free of charge. Caveats: the forecast is a narrative bulletin, not a downloadable time series, so archives would need to be kept by the user. It supports hazard exposure and emergency response planning for power grids, satellites, aviation and GNSS in the face of space weather; related records are the ESA Space Weather Service Network and the Australian World Data Centre for space weather.
